turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, yeah, nice to meet you too. I guess what really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. Like, I’ll be sitting at the bench—I make jewelry, mostly custom pieces, which is usually great but the price of silver has been doing some really weird things lately. My buddy was just telling me about this guy who buys scrap metal down on 4th street, and anyway... I’ll be at the bench, and I'll jump from reading a customer email to looking at a saw mark on a ring, and then I'll hear some random noise outside. There's this stray dog that keeps knocking over the trash cans by my shop, it's honestly driving me crazy and animal control does nothing. But yeah, by the time I look back down at my desk, I realize I’ve completely lost the whole work order. I just don't know where my head is at.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have trouble paying attention as a child?
turns.patient_response: As a kid? Um, no, I don't think so. I don't remember anyone ever saying I had trouble paying attention back then. I got through high school fine. Shop class was my favorite, obviously, since that's how I got into metalwork in the first place. My teacher, Mr. Henderson, he had this crazy old vintage truck he was always fixing up in the back of the lot. A Chevy, I think? It was painted this really ugly shade of green, like... almost like a split pea soup color. I never understood why people paint cars green. Like, silver or black just looks so much cleaner. Silver is so hard to keep polished though, especially if it sits in the display case too long, it just tarnishes if the humidity is off in the shop... wait, what did you ask me? Something about when I was younger?

turns.doctor_question: Have there been times when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, actually, a while back there was this stretch where I felt amazing. I was sleeping maybe two, three hours a night, tops. But I’d wake up totally clear-headed, just buzzing and excited to start cutting stones or posting new designs online way before the sun even came up. The sunrise from my shop window is actually pretty incredible. It catches the dust in the air—which reminds me, I really need to change the filter on my ventilation system. If you don't keep up with that, the silver dust just coats everything. I had this one customer bring in a family heirloom, a real nice turquoise piece, but the setting was completely shot. Turquoise is so soft, you know? You have to be super careful or you'll crack it right down the middle. I usually source my turquoise from this guy in Arizona, he drives it up himself in this old van. He’s got this dog that rides shotgun, a little terrier mix... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, I wasn't sleeping much at all, but I felt great.

turns.doctor_question: During that period when you were sleeping only a few hours and felt amazing, did it cause serious problems in your life or work?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, it did actually. I ended up missing a major custom delivery, which was really bad. It was supposed to be this intricate anniversary piece, and the guy wanted it shipped directly to his wife's office. Shipping things right now is such a nightmare anyway, the post office down the street from me always has a line out the door. The lady who works the counter there, Brenda, she collects those vintage stamps, which is kinda cool, but she will talk your ear off if you let her. I swear I spent twenty minutes there once just listening to her explain the 1980 winter olympics commemorative series. 

But anyway, my shop records just got completely disorganized during that whole stretch. I had invoices and sketches everywhere, so I actually had to stop taking new work for now just to try and figure out what was going on. It’s frustrating because I like staying busy, but I just couldn't keep track of who paid for what. 

And my family has been checking on me way more than usual, too. They got all worried because they said I’d slipped so far from my regular routines. My mom keeps coming by the shop and bringing over these big Tupperware containers of lasagna. I mean, I like lasagna, but she uses that really chunky tomato sauce... I'm more of a smooth sauce guy, you know? Like, if you blend it first it coats the pasta way better, plus the chunks just get stuck in the corners of the container when you try to wash it. But yeah, I guess things got pretty messy at the shop for a bit.

turns.doctor_question: During that stretch, did you feel more confident or powerful than usual?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually, I did. Like, I won this ribbon at a local craft show around that time, and it just... it made me feel like I’d finally proved I was on a completely different level, you know? Like I was untouchable. I felt like I could take on every single custom order that came my way and turn each one into this massive showpiece that no one else around here could even come close to. 

Craft shows are so weird though, honestly. You have to set up your booth so early, and the lighting in those convention centers is always terrible. It's this awful fluorescent hum that totally washes out the silver. I tried bringing my own LED spotlights once, but the extension cord situation was a nightmare. This guy next to me, he was selling these handmade leather belts, and he kept tripping over my cord. He had this huge belt buckle on, shaped like a longhorn skull. I don't know who actually wears those, they seem so heavy. Like, wouldn't that just pull your pants down all day? You'd have to wear suspenders with it, I guess. My grandpa used to wear suspenders, the kind that button into the waistband, not the clip-on ones... what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah, I just felt really, really confident about my work. Like I was the best.

turns.doctor_question: During that energized stretch, did you have any experiences like hearing or seeing things other people didn't, or believing something that others said wasn't true?
turns.patient_response:
No, no, nothing like that. I didn't see anything weird or hear voices or anything, and I didn't have any crazy ideas that weren't real. I mean, my ideas for the jewelry were real, just maybe a little too ambitious. 

Speaking of ambitious, I tried to make this one piece out of pure copper wire once. Copper is so tricky because it oxidizes so fast, you know? It turns your skin green if you don't seal it right. I read online that you can use clear nail polish to seal it, but that just flakes off after a couple of days. My sister uses this really expensive top coat for her nails, she gets it imported from Japan or something. She's super into nail art. Last week she had these tiny little rhinestones glued to every single nail. I don't know how she types on her phone with those things. I tried texting her about a family dinner and she sent back a bunch of typos, probably because of the rhinestones. We were supposed to go to this Mexican place down the street, but they closed down. It's a shame, they had the best guacamole. They used real cotija cheese on top... wait, sorry. No, I didn't have any of those weird experiences you're talking about. Just the energy and the ideas.

turns.doctor_question: About how long did that high-energy period last?
turns.patient_response: It started right after I got that jewelry-show award, actually. They gave me this big blue ribbon, which was cool, but it was made of that really cheap stiff satin material. You know the kind that frays at the edges if you just look at it wrong? I actually wanted to frame it for the shop, so I went to this big box craft store down on 4th street. Have you ever tried to get something custom framed? It is unbelievably expensive. They wanted like eighty bucks just for the cardboard matting. And then they try to upsell you on the UV-protective museum glass. Like, it's a ribbon, not the Mona Lisa, right? But the guy working the counter was super pushy about it. He had this little mustache that kind of twitched when he talked. He actually reminded me a lot of my high school metal shop teacher, Mr. Henderson. He used to make us wear these giant scratched-up safety goggles that always fogged up the second you started the blowtorch... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, how long it lasted. Right. Yeah, that whole wired, out-of-control stretch went on for about two weeks.
